- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” factor — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges mean reversion; align forecast with recent 7–14 day moving average instead of long-term trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 5-day weighted average of sentiment-adjusted history.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model often fails to capture subtle mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 10-day prices as baseline.
